articles.title: La china en el zapato de Tesla vuelve al ataque: BYD desafía al Semi entre los camiones eléctricos
articles.standfirst: Lanza el BYD ETT 44, una cabeza tractora que supera los números del Tesla Semi
articles.summary: Lanza el BYD ETT 44, una cabeza tractora que supera los números del Tesla Semi
articles.body: El mayor fabricante de vehículos eléctricos del planeta, la china BYD, no quiere dejarle a su mayor rival, la norteamericana Tesla, espacio libre en ningún segmento de mercado. tampoco en el de los camiones eléctricos, donde la marca de Elon Musk se dispone a lanzar su modelo Semi también en Europa. De hecho, BYD ha sido la gran protagonista del IAA Transportation 2026 de Hannover, el salón más importante de vehículos comerciales en el continente, con su primer camión eléctrico: el BYD ETT 44 Se trata de una cabeza tractora de alta potencia y capacidad de recarga ultrarrápida concebida, como no puede ser de otro modo, para recorrer las largas distancias de las rutas comerciales de transporte. De hecho, el ETT 44 tiene más de 1.000 CV de potencia. Aunque BYD no especifica la cifra final, asegura que será "la mayor de su segmento" (el Tesla Semi homologará en Europa 1.087). En cuanto a autonomía, el digito que aporta la marca china es de "hasta 600 kilómetros" (por los 550 del Tesla Semi). Donde BYD marcará la diferencia con el sello de Elon Musk es en la potencia de carga, un elemento clave en estos gigantes de la ruta. El BYD ETT 44 equipará una batería capaz de aprovechar al máximo los 1,5 MW de los puntos de recarga Flash Charging que la marca china va a empezar a desplegar en Europa ya desde este mismo año. Eso le permitirá recuperar, en apenas 20 minutos, la energía necesaria para recorrer otros 400 kilómetros. BYD también presume de otros atributos en su ETT 44: un diseño moderno, tecnología de vanguardia en cuanto a asistentes de conducción, seguridad (5 estrellas EuroNCAP) y lo más importante: es capaz de reducir el Coste Total de Movilidad (CTM) respecto a sus equivalentes diésel.

articles.title: New York Giants' Francis Mauigoa ready to face the man he once idolized
articles.summary: New York Giants rookie OL Francis Mauigoa once idolized Aaron Donald, and now he'll face him on Monday night.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams legendary defensive tackle and future Hall of Famer Aaron Donald returns to the field on Monday night against the New York Giants after two years away.

Waiting for him will be Giants rookie guard Francis "Sisi" Mauigoa, the 10th overall selection in this year's NFL draft, who, like many young players, idolized Donald growing up.

Donald, 35, retired after the 2023 season and is said to be in game shape. He will have to be. Mauigoa is one of the league's promising new stars. This game will be a battle for everyone to focus on.

Mauigoa, who stands 6-foot-6, weighs 330 pounds, and plays with a chip on his shoulder, is ready.

"It's going to be a tough challenge," Mauigoa told NJ Advance Media this week . "The best opponent I'll ever go against in my whole life, I guess."

"I mean, he's Aaron Donald. People lose sleep from him. Obviously, I have the utmost respect for him. He's still going to be him. He's still going to be a game wrecker, somebody that can change the game."

Asked if he was losing sleep over facing Donald, Sisi said he wasn't.

"Nah," he said. "I usually go in with a neutral mentality. I adopted this when I was at Miami — nameless, faceless. It doesn't matter who you're facing. You've just got to trust your own technique and your own playing style."

That being said, Mauigoa feels he knows what to expect from Donald.

"He's going to be the type of guy that is going to do whatever he wants to do," Mauigoa said. "It can be a pain in the ass. But he made a name for himself with it — a person that doesn't have a tap-out button. He'll keep going and keep going."

articles.title: Florida State’s lack of depth underscores poor offseason personnel decisions
articles.summary: The last two games have shown the Seminoles’ ongoing roster building flaws.
articles.body:
Florida State finally looked like the team the coaching staff promised in the offseason.

Ashton Daniels and the offense moved the ball downfield at will as the Seminoles scored touchdowns on three of their first four drives. On defense, Tony White miraculously forced Alabama into three-and-outs on their first two drives. The Noles led 21-6 and had the Tide facing a third-and-17 with four minutes to go in the first half.

Then, the next 34 minutes of game action happened.

FSU's defense allowed points on nine straight drives as the personnel melted down and the coaching staff couldn't adjust. On offense, the Noles finished the game with explosive plays but poor game management, resulting in two touchdowns, two turnovers, and a lifeline for Alabama to get back in the contest at the end of the first half. Ultimately, the performance wasn't good enough, no matter how the game started.

The Seminoles had an extra week to prepare, while Alabama returned from an SEC road game. But once the Tide got their feet under them and made adjustments, they went on a 37-7 run, with no answers from the Florida State coaching staff.

"We have to be able to get off the field, and we showed the capability early in the game," a dejected Mike Norvell said after the game. "We allowed too many explosive plays tonight. … As their run game got going later in the game, it did wear on us.

"Not good enough when you give up over 550 yards of offense."

Of course, as with everything related to Florida State this season, you can't look at it in a vacuum. Poor offseason personnel decisions left the team lacking depth, especially on defense. The Seminoles held Alabama to 13 yards on 10 rushes in the first quarter and then allowed 124 yards on 14 carries in the fourth quarter.

No example better displayed the lack of bodies than Alabama's final touchdown drive of the game. FSU pulled within seven and backed the Crimson Tide up to their own 10-yard line thanks to a holding penalty. Kalen DeBoer's team proceeded to run the ball on eight of the next nine plays, including a 20-yard touchdown run, to close out the game. Once again, Florida State's defensive line lacked playmakers, with no sacks and only three tackles for loss from the front seven in yesterday's game, and was worn out by the end.

."It really has nothing to do with effort or want to," linebacker Chris Jones told the media postgame. "It has to do with execution. They came out with different things, and we did not execute the right way. … They came out with more of a gap scheme at the beginning of the game. Then, they started running more stretch and outside zone.

"We were in bad spots in a lot of those plays."

The big-money defensive acquisitions have not delivered for the Noles. The Seminoles brought in new coach Nick Williams to coach the edges and help ease the load on defensive line coach Terrance Knighton. Nobody on the defensive front seems to have taken a step forward this year. The Desir twins, who FSU paid to keep out of the transfer portal, are being asked to play more than they should because of the lack of depth and finished the game with a combined 0.5 tackles for loss and no sacks. Up the middle, Daniel Lyons has yet to take over a game the way the coaching staff hoped, and the players behind him, Kevin Wynn and Jordan Sanders, aren't providing enough to spell him. The defensive front did a good job containing Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell early in the game with rush-lane integrity, but his 57-yard touchdown run felt like the death blow in the third quarter.

"There was an element late where we definitely got worn down and being on the field," Norvell lamented. "There were a few times when we had a self-inflicted miss in alignment. There are big plays when no edge shows up.

"I thought we defended the run really well early, and it was unfortunate to see where it went to."

Even if it was more apparent on defense, Florida State's lack of offensive depth showed in the second half, too. After Norvell's well-designed early-game scripts, the Noles struggled to match that impact later. FSU's offensive line, which inserted Paul Bowling at right guard and kept Nate Pabst at right tackle, struggled to keep Ashton Daniels upright with a clean pocket to throw and create open rushing lanes.

Part of that also fell on Daniels, who struggled to process the field quickly, but the Seminoles still rushed for under four yards per carry (3.6) with sack yardage taken out. Norvell's offense moved the ball on big plays, as 344 of Daniels' 377 passing yards came on 10 plays, but the Seminoles lack the talent to push defenses back drive after drive.

"We had some missed opportunities on drives on offense that we have to have. You come on the road in a hostile environment against a good football team, you have to capitalize on those," Norvell said.

A little over a year ago, the Seminoles convincingly defeated Alabama and made 2024 feel like a blip. Yesterday, the Tide spotted Florida State 15 points and still won by two touchdowns. The program's decline is obvious, and poor evaluations and portal pickups are a major reason for it.

articles.title: 2026 Mountain West Football Week 3 Recap
articles.summary: Expected blowouts, standout performances, and a descent into the depths of Hell highlighted the MW slate in Week 3.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 season is in the books, and it was a lot milder for the Mountain West as a whole. The limited slate of games saw just two one-score contests, one of which saw a known contender assert themselves as a national threat, and the other seeing a hopeful contender sinking straight back into being an embarrassment to their fans. Without further ado, let's get into the MW slate in Week 3.

The Scoop: There is but one takeaway from a performance like this: Jay Sawvel is as good as gone in Laramie. Entering this game, Central Michigan had just narrowly beaten FCS team Colgate by scoring just 13 points, serving up the second worst offense in the country in terms of yardage. The Chips proceeded to have their best game of the season by far against the Cowboys, beating Wyoming by 14 in a game that was nowhere near as close as the final score would indicate.

Central Michigan had their way with Wyoming on the ground, carrying the ball 59 times for a whopping 339 yards and three touchdowns. QB Angel Flores, while completing just four passes for 32 yards, was still the engine of the offense, racking up 28 carries for 163 yards and two of those touchdowns. Flores' counterpart, Tyler Hughes, was absolutely abhorrent on the day, completing just 14 of 30 passes for 173 yards and two interceptions.

Wyoming was able to somewhat get the run game going, averaging 5.8 YPC on their 28 carries, but a sizeable portion of that production came after the Cowboys went down 24-3 at the end of the third quarter. To be precise, 193 of Wyoming's 342 total yards came in the fourth quarter, once the Chippewas were simply playing to close the game out. There is no way to spin this outcome that is not a complete embarrassment for Wyoming, which now looks like it will be one of the worst teams in the country this season.

Wyoming (1-2) will travel back home to Laramie for their conference opener next week, hosting the equally struggling Hawaii Rainbow Warriors (1-2, 0-1 MW) on Sept. 26 at 1:00 p.m. MDT. Hawaii was on a bye this week, but had finally gotten their season back on track somewhat with a win over New Mexico State the week before. This will be a battle of who wants to lose more, which by the looks of things will end up being the Cowboys. There will almost certainly be a coaching change before the end of the season here.

The Scoop: This game ended up being a tale of two halves. In the first half, UTEP took it to Michigan in the Big House, consistently exposing the Wolverines ' many flaws. The Miners capitalized on two Michigan fumbles to put themselves up 14-7 midway through the second quarter, sparking dreams of a miracle upset, shades of 2007 Appalachian State. Unfortunately, after that, the Miners had just 32 yards of offense the rest of the way, all while Michigan scored on every single remaining drive, save for kneeling out the end of the game. UTEP played admirably for a while, but once Michigan started taking the game somewhat seriously, there was very little the Miners could actually do.

UTEP (1-2) will travel back to El Paso for an important nonconference contest next week, hosting the Oregon State Beavers (1-2) on Sept. 26 at 7:00 p.m. MDT. Oregon State started their season off with two straight losses, albeit both competitive contests against top-25 teams. OSU is led by an explosive offense, highlighted by the nation's leading receiver, freshman Jesse Legree. UTEP likely won't keep this one very close, but it is an important contest nonetheless.

The Scoop: Turns out the Western Kentucky game was nothing more than an enormous fluke after all. Jeff Choke made his triumphant return, as the Wolf Pack blew a fourth-quarter lead with a cavalcade of bad play-calling and stupid mistakes, losing to Middle Tennessee by one score for the second year in a row. This game went the exact way I expected, the only difference was the fact that MTSU got one more field goal than I expected them to.

Carter Jones made his return from his dubious injury, accounting for 212 yards of offense, a rushing TD, and a terrible interception at the Blue Raiders' 11-yard line that killed a potential scoring drive in the third quarter. Nevada also fumbled twice inside their own 30-yard line, both of which led to Blue Raider touchdowns. In addition, the Pack had a Gerick Robinson punt return TD overturned due to an unnecessary holding penalty away from the ball. To be frank, however, Nevada would have never been in this game at all if not for several MTSU penalties, the vast majority of which were on third down.

Nevada averaged just 2.2 YPC on their 34 rush attempts, weighed down heavily by several disastrous jet sweeps, as well as a 4th and 2 run up the gut in the fourth quarter that sealed Nevada's long-obvious fate. Even without those terrible plays, the Wolf Pack would have still wound up stifled by MTSU's defense, which racked up four TFLs and a sack-fumble on Jones. I haven't even mentioned Nevada's defense being destroyed by MTSU's backfield, which racked up 157 rushing yards and just one play for negative yards all night long.

Nevada is now a disgusting 3-10 in one-score games in the last three seasons. This was simply a performance going back to classic Nevada under Jeff Choate, whose seat would be flaming-hot if not for the fact that the university already has a massive buyout to pay out due to their last failure of a head coaching hire. Just another day in Reno, I guess.

Nevada (1-2) will travel back to Northern Nevada to host Air Force (1-1, 0-1 MW) for their conference opener on Sept. 26 at 7:30 p.m. PDT. The Pack have not beaten the Falcons since 2018, and Air Force was blown out by North Dakota State in their conference opener, but given Coach Choate's previous comments about revenge games, Nevada will be playing with zero extra passion, execution, or urgency in this contest. Air Force has shown typically excellent ability to run the ball with their triple-option offense, which does not bode well for Nevada, given how they were ripped apart on the ground last night. No matter what, this game will result in yet another one-score loss

The Scoop: I predicted New Mexico would keep it very close with Oklahoma in this one, and they did exactly that. On a night dominated by defense, the Lobos trailed just 7-6 at halftime, forcing John Mateer into mistake after mistake while completely shutting down OU's run game. Unfortunately, UNM's offense never got going in this one, going scoreless in the second half to walk away with a hard-fought, yet ultimately disappointing 14-6 loss. The Lobos' defense is going to be a problem this season, and they deserve a medal for how they shut down the Sooners' offense in this game. They forced four puntes, three turnovers, a sack, and six TFLs on the night, keeping the OU offense in check all night.

New Mexico's biggest problem was their cycle of quarterback hokey-pokey continuing in this match, as Teo Fa'avae and Luke Moga each completed four passes for a combined 116 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions. This allowed OU's defense to focus on the run, averaging just 1.6 YPC on the Lobos' 38 attempts. One of New Mexico's offensive lapses was particularly painful, as the Lobos got the ball at Oklahoma's 39-yard line after a muffed punt, only to go three-and-out with -1 yards on the drive. Get something on that drive and maybe UNM's game-ending turnover on downs looks a little bit different. Nonetheless, the Lobos have arrived in the national spotlight. They are frontrunners for the CFP in 2026, especially if they can get their offense sorted out.

New Mexico (2-1) will travel back to the Land of Enchantment next weekend, only they won't be going to Albuquerque. Instead, they will be heading down south to take on loathed in-state rivals New Mexico State (1-2) on Sept. 26 at 1:30 p.m. MDT. NMSU was on a bye this week, with their previous game being a 10-point loss at Hawaii. The Aggies should be no threat to the Lobos given the latter's level of performance this season, but that doesn't mean that they will be shown any mercy in this contest.

The Scoop: I'll give the Huskies some credit here, they played much better than I expected they would. NIU was clearly playing mad early in this one, jumping out to a 10-0 lead while outgaining the Wildcats 106 to minus-five. After that, the Wildcats went on a 42-0 run that involved QB Noah Fifita breaking Arizona's all-time passing record, going 31-of-34 for 325 yards with four TDs and no INTs. In his first start as a Huskie, Taron Dickens completed 25 passes for 228 yards and a TD with no turnovers, so there is certainly potential offensively. I will need to see more from the Huskies' defense to truly believe in their ability to win in the Mountain West, but games like this where they actually show some life give me far more hope than their blowout loss to Iowa. Good game, NIU. You're getting there.

NIU (0-3) will complete their nonconference schedule with a trip to Atlanta, GA to take on the Georgia State Panthers (2-1) on Sept. 26 at 1:00 p.m. CDT. Whereas the Panthers would normally be a total pushover, they are off to a hot start this season, taking down reigning C-USA champion Kennesaw State on the road and giving UCF more than their fair share this weekend. This would be a big win for the Huskies if they can pull it off.

The Scoop: A great bounceback win here for UTEP, who took their frustrations out on poor Texas Southern, destroying them for the game's last 35 minutes. After the Tigers took the lead, 10-7 in the second quarter, the Miners scored the game's final 44 points for a convincing win via rout. E.J. Colson threw for 239 yards and four touchdowns, while the Miners' 33 carries resulted in 252 yards and three touchdowns. Tiger QBs were held to just 99 passing yards and an interception, and Texas Southern's offense was held to just 34 yards after taking their 10-7 lead. This was a typical FCS win, but an impressive one for the Miners nonetheless.

UTEP (1-1) will travel next week to Ann Arbor, MI to take on the Michigan Wolverines at 1:30 p.m. MDT on Big Ten Network. Michigan's official record is 2-0, but the college football world, AP voters, and basic logic and reason state that they lost their home opener to Western Michigan before taking down a struggling Oklahoma the next week. UTEP already was blown out by the Sooners, so playing the Wolverines will likely not bring better results to the fans in El Paso.

The Scoop: One may look at the 21-point margin of victory here and say that Sac State performed better against the Bison than expected, but I'd say this has more to do with NDSU offensive sluggishness in the second half than anything the Hornets pulled on the field. Nathan Hayes completed just 14 of 24 passes, and the Bison only had 362 yards of offense, but one must also consider the fact that the Bison led 28-0 with 11:24 left in the second quarter and ask whether NDSU was even trying after that. This was a thorough beatdown, but NDSU never pulled their starters so I supposed the Hornets have earned a slight pat on the back for that. The Bison, meanwhile, look just as imposing a threat to the Mountain West as they have all season. The CFP is a real possibility now.

North Dakota State finally has their first bye week of the season this week, returning when they host their first home conference game against Wyoming (1-2) on Oct. 3 at 2:30 p.m. CDT. Wyoming is a terrible team on the verge of firing their coach, so I have no problem believing that this will be an utter rout with the Bison having a full week to prepare.

The Scoop: Finally, we have the game that you can't help but wish had been better than it was. The first 50 minutes of this game were a defensive showcase, with neither team's quarterback ever looking comfortable. The Bulldogs led 6-3 at the half, and the game was 13-10 after a SJSU touchdown in the fourth quarter. After that, however, the Spartans had two interceptions and two turnovers on downs on their last four drives, making the final score look far worse than it actually was.

The two teams were evenly matched in nearly every statistical category, save for turnovers, where the Spartans lost the battle (and the game) 4-0. Luke Weaver threw for 244 yards and a TD, but had a dreadful four interceptions against a 'Dogs defense that had just one on the season prior to this game. Worse yet, three of the four picks were on deep balls thrown inside Fresno State's 40-yard line, killing all momentum SJSU had at the worst possible times. Probably the more alarming stat was Jabari Bates going for just 94 yards on 19 carries, showcasing the main way the Bulldogs found to beat the Spartans: you beat Bates, you beat San Jose State. At least Anthony Ivey (7-for-150) starred at wideout, but that's about as comforting as a blanket made out of a cactus at this point. This was nothing short of total deflation for San Jose State, which is a bad thing to happen at the outset of conference play.

San Jose State (2-2) will have their first bye week of the season this week, preparing for a trip to Honolulu to face Hawaii (1-2, 0-1 MW) on Oct. 3 at 9:00 p.m. PDT. Hawaii has had their fair share of struggles as of late, so perhaps a trip for Luke Weaver to face the freshman that beat him out for the starting job a year ago will motivate this team to come out swinging. Hopefully for Spartan fans' sakes, those swings don't lead to a high turnover count this time.

articles.title: Michigan Football freshman edge rusher Tariq Boney impresses vs UTEP
articles.summary: While he didn’t see the field much in the first two games, Tariq Boney made his presence felt for Michigan Football in Week 3:
articles.body:
The college football world has officially been introduced to Tariq Boney. Michigan's freshman edge rusher had only one snap in the first two weeks of the season, but ended Week 3 against UTEP with four total tackles, including 1.5 TFLs and one sack.

Before his formal introduction to the college football world, Boney's name circulated around the media, as he was often mentioned by head coach Kyle Whittingham and defensive coordinator Jay Hill for having a great fall camp.

On multiple occasions leading up to the first game, Whittingham and Hill praised Boney, as well as his freshman edge rushing counterpart Carter Meadows who has been dealing with injuries and made his first career appearance against UTEP.

On August 21, Whittingham said "Two freshman defensive ends, Carter Meadows and Tariq Boney, are having an outstanding camp, and they're gonna be involved."

Hill on August 26 said "Tariq Boney and Carter Meadows have done unbelievable things for freshmen," and emphasized a similar sentiment on September 2, saying "as a young freshman, has really done some great things."

In Boney's lone snap against the Sooners, he came off the right side and bulldozed past the offensive lineman. Boney's rush forced quarterback John Mateer to step up in the pocket to avoid the pressure and escape a sack.

UTEP quarterback EJ Colson Jr. didn't have the same luck against Boney.

Near the end of the third quarter, Boney lined up in the same spot he did in the play against Oklahoma. He bulldozed past the offensive lineman yet again, avoided the pick-up block from the running back and sacked Colson.

"His quickness, his explosion, he is a powerful guy," Whittingham said after Michigan took down UTEP 52-17. "He's built like a fire hydrant and strong as an ox in the weight room. Just his strength and explosion is as good as I've ever seen in a true freshman. … He's got a very developed body and relentless motor. His motor never shuts down. He's constantly in pursuit."

Boney proved his ability to produce constant pursuit, coming up with 1.5 TFLs in addition to his first-career sack. Boney was in a group of 12 Wolverines who recorded at least 0.5 TFLs on the day, and Boney tied for the lead on the team with 1.5 TFLs alongside sophomore Benny Patterson III.

This type of performance, despite being his first significant playing time on a Saturday, was not unexpected from his teammates.

"It's definitely in line with what I've seen in practice," sophomore Chase Taylor said. "He played for sure because you can see that he's got the size, talent, build, speed. It's just coming together."

As a true freshman, Boney is starting to make a name for himself with a stellar performance against the Miners. And if Saturday was any indication, it's going to be hard to keep Boney off the field in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Three takeaways from UNC’s wildly frustrating loss to Clemson
articles.summary: The Heels now have some big issue to sort out during the bye week.
articles.body:
I'm not even sure where to begin. When Clemson punted with 7:06 left in the 2nd quarter, Carolina ran it back to the Clemson 46 while holding a 17-3 lead. A 14-point lead, with the ball in field position that often results in points, had UNC fans feeling confident. To that point in the game and season, Clemson's offense was 4-33 on third downs and had scored one touchdown. UNC already had 195 yards of offense, including 112 on the ground. The game seemed headed towards a UNC romp.

From that point forward, Clemson would outscore UNC 25-3 and outgain the Tar Heels by 218 yards. Clemson's comeback started slowly, gathered momentum, and then ended emphatically after a three hour weather delay.

Billy Edwards may have lost his job as UNC's starting quarterback

You can blame me for Edwards' meltdown. Midway through the second quarter, I contributed to the staff chat this observation: "Won't be this game, but Billy Edwards' inability to to hit downfield is going to be a problem." To that point, Edwards had misfired on several downfield attempts to Shipp and Thurman, but the efficiency coming from the run game and short passing game had the offense moving the ball.

Edwards' accuracy with longer throws was a concern coming into the game. Against TCU and ETSU, Edwards was 21-23 on throws travelling less than 10 yards downfield but only 10-24 on throws deeper than that. After the first quarter, Clemson adjusted, compressing their coverage and putting more pressure on the pocket. Their goal was clear — make Billy Edwards beat them with his arm on longer throws. And he couldn't.

From the point in the first half that UNC had the ball at the Clemson 46 up 17-3, Edwards stat line was 7-16 for 56 yards and an interception. Edwards for the day finished 13-30 for 152 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Against this same Clemson defense, LSU threw for 334 yards, and Georgia Southern's Max Johnson — yes, that Max Johnson — threw for 244. Edwards' inability over three games to connect downfield consistently, with weapons like Jelani Thurman and Jordan Shipp at his disposal, was a fatal flaw against Clemson, one likely to be just as fatal against the rest of ACC competition.

Bill Belichick has a lot of thinking to do about his quarterback position. The question isn't whether or not Edwards can elevate his game. It's whether UNC has anyone in the QB room capable of performing better.

Clemson's fast pace exposed UNC's defensive depth and communication

UNC was down Melkart Abou Jaoude for this game. One aspect of depth is having a "next man up" at key positions. For MAJ, that's Donovan Hoilette, who transferred from FCS Richmond. Hoilette finished the day with two tackles, and Clemson found some success working his edge in the run game. Hoilette contributed no sacks or QB pressures. Missing MAJ hurt.

The other aspect of depth is dealing with teams that will try to run pace, and Clemson enjoyed a lot of success when trying to move fast against Belichick's defense. Clemson worked with pace on its final first half drive that ended with a field goal and sent the game into halftime down 17-6. The drive took over five minutes, but Clemson ran 18 plays and moved the ball 88 yards, going 3-4 on third downs. Clemson's true freshman QB, Tait Reynolds, looked much more comfortable operating in that mode. Clemson kept it up in the 2nd half, averaging 7.3 yards per rush and 13.9 per pass attempt.

Initially, it appeared that physical fatigue might be the most significant issue with the pace, as UNC's defense seemed gassed by the time weather put a halt to the game midway through the fourth quarter. However, after that three hour delay, Clemson's first possession went 68 yards in four plays. It appears that moving quickly short-circuited defensive communication, both between the sidelines and the defensive captain as well as among the players on the field.

Expect to see more of this from opponents until UNC figures out the communication and substitution issues exposed by Clemson's pace of play.

In two P4 games now, Bobby Petrino's offense disappears after the first quarter

UNC against TCU and Clemson scored 24 points in the opening frame. In the succeeding six quarters of play, UNC's offense has managed all of nine points. In the first quarter against TCU, UNC averaged 7.42 yards per play on 19 plays. Against Clemson in the first, UNC averaged 6.7 yards per play on 19 plays. In the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th quarters of those two games, UNC has averaged 4.56 yards per play. UNC's 2-11 on third down conversions in the second half of those games. Any way you cut it, the offense starts hot and then somehow turns into last year's offense.

The play-calling, long considered Petrino's wheelhouse, was odd at times in this game as well. For the moment, we'll begin and end with the 4th and one play late that sealed UNC's fate. Edwards' struggles with accuracy the further downfield the play design were noted above. UNC needed a yard to sustain a drive that had to end in points. Petrino called for a play action shot deep downfield to Jelani Thurman, a play which didn't fool Clemson and a pass from Edwards that gave Thurman no chance at making a catch or drawing a flag.

With only a two game sample to work with, the overly simple explanation appears to be that Petrino's initial game plan works spectacularly well. Then, opponents adjust, and UNC has no answers to the adjustments. The QB issues noted above contribute to that, but unless Belichick is forcing his hand, Petrino's chosen the QB he feels represents UNC's best chance to win games.

Bill Belichick's team collapsed against Clemson . The remote chance remains that Clemson rips through much of its remaining schedule in the same way it ripped through UNC after finding its footing late in the first half. However, Clemson's success came through superior scheme and execution, not overwhelming talent. The Tar Heels' future opponents were taking notes. With a bye week to prepare for Notre Dame, Belichick has two weeks to figure out how to not let that game be completely embarrassing. Then, Belichick has get back on the winning side of football games in UNC's final eight. If he doesn't, those will be the final eight games of Belichick's coaching career.

articles.title: 2 Cowboys to buy, 2 to sell versus the Commanders
articles.summary: Today is very important.
articles.body:
Week 2 is here, and the Dallas Cowboys are looking for a bounce-back week after a tough loss to the New York football Giants . Let's look at some players to buy/sell for Week 2.

Pickens almost feels like a given. He had some massive drops against the Giants; one might have been a touchdown. As is often the criticism of Pickens, his focus and intensity might not always be at 100%. His Week 1 stat line is marginal. Three catches for 28 yards on six targets. He drew more penalty yardage than actual receiving yards, racking up 38 total yards on Giants penalties. So even on an off night, he still made an impact.

What's more, Pickens led the Cowboys with a 16.1-yard average depth of target and 37.9% of the team's air yards, signaling the kind of role the Cowboys see for him.

Washington offers a logical bounce-back opportunity. The Commanders' secondary is already dealing with the absence of Trey Amos , while Washington cornerback Mike Sainristil was criticized heavily for a poor Week 1 performance. Saying Pickens is "due" for a bounce-back seems cliché, but Week 2 could very well be that moment for the 2025 Pro Bowler.

Ferguson had a tough game in Week 1. He only had six yards on two catches while being targeted six times against the G-Men. Dallas views the TE position like they do their running backs. A well-rounded player who can block and make plays. With Washington bringing an aggressive defensive scheme, Dallas can't afford to have its tight end become a liability when he's attached to the formation.

Then you have to consider the rise of Brevyn Spann-Ford and the many receivers that Dak Prescott has at his disposal. Ferguson's impact seems capped at occasional catches, and without some of the flash he could have shown, there may not be enough room for him to have a huge impact. Even still, the Commanders just gave up a huge game to Dallas Goedert , so anything could happen.

Ezeiruaku was arguably the Cowboys' best defender in Week 1. Yes, he had moments when he lost discipline on the edge and struggled in coverage, but he finished with 10 tackles, a half-sack, a tackle for loss and two pressures, and Dallas' official site notes that he earned the team's highest PFF grade at 86.5.

Now look at the matchup. Washington's starting left tackle is Brandon Coleman , filling in for injured Laremy Tunsil . Coleman allowed seven pressures and a sack against Philadelphia , while Washington's starting tackles allowed 15 pressures combined.

On top of that, Commanders QB Jayden Daniels tends to hold onto the ball too long. Daniels took a league-leading 3.41 seconds to throw in Week 1. That's a gift to a pass rush that desperately needs to get home. Ezeiruaku showed in Week 1 that he can create disruption. Week 2 gives him an opportunity to turn that disruption into production.

There are so many questions surrounding this group, and now that Overshown is out, even more doubt can creep into that position group. Dallas gave up 165 rushing yards to the Giants in Week 1, and the defense allowed New York to convert 82% of its third downs. The linebacking group was part of a larger defensive problem: Dallas struggled to consistently fit the run and communicate in coverage.

Now rookie third-round pick Jaishawn Barham will take over at MIKE and wear the green dot in his second NFL game. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Barham has "great command" of the defense, but that's still a significant responsibility for a rookie.

The problem is that Washington presents a similar challenge to Jaxson Dart and the Giants. Jayden Daniels is a mobile quarterback. Washington also ran for 132 yards against Philadelphia, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt carrying 16 times for 63 yards and Daniels adding 31 yards. That means Dallas' linebackers will have to diagnose quickly while also accounting for the quarterback as a runner.

And that's before you factor in the loss of Overshown, who normally relays Christian Parker's calls to the defense. Parker said this week that he trusts Barham, Dee Winters and Shemar James to step into the role, but the Cowboys will clearly be asking more of that trio than they expected entering the season.

Can Dallas' linebackers clean up their Week 1 mistakes while also replacing the guy who was supposed to run the defense? A significant ask at this point.

articles.title: Explosive! Cowboys paths to Week 2 victory revealed
articles.summary: If the Cowboys want to beat the Commanders, they need better special teams play, better third-down defense, and more explosive plays on offense.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders are both 0-1, coming off division losses. Each team will be desperate to avoid falling into a 0-2 NFC East hole, especially the Cowboys as they are at home. The Commanders have a mobile quarterback in Jayden Daniels , similar to Jaxson Dart . Otherwise, they aren't comparable to the New York Giants roster, so the issues New York created for the Dallas defense won't be the same.

The Dallas defense was the main issue in Week 1. Whether it was a matchup problem or they're just a bad unit, but a win for the Cowboys in Week 2 will be more about all three phases than the defense. The offense has to be better facing a poor defensive opponent and the special teams must resolve their field-position issues. Here are the keys to a Dallas victory over the Commanders.

The lack of explosive plays against the Giants might have been the biggest shock from that contest . An explosive play is a 10-yard rush or a 20-yard pass. With options like CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , and Ryan Flournoy for Dak Prescott to throw to, explosive passes should be regular for them, but they didn't have a single reception for 20 yards.

The rushing attack had minimal explosive plays last season, so not having many isn't surprising, but the running backs had zero. The only explosive play for the Cowboys in Week 1 was a 10-yard scramble by Prescott. Dallas has to attack the Washington defense with a downfield passing attack, and hopefully explosive runs can develop as they wear down the Washington defense.

The Cowboys' offense had the second-best third-down conversion rate of opening week, but the problem is the only team ahead of them was their opponent, the Giants. New York was 9-for-10 on third-down conversions before a kneel-down on a third down at the end of the game. They weren't thought of as a juggernaut, but the Cowboys defense made them look like one.

The Giants converted four plays of third-and-9 or longer, and the only unsuccessful play of that kind was the kneel-down to end the game. This is as obvious as it can get for any team, for any week, but if Dallas allows anywhere close to the same success rate on third down to the Commanders, they'll end the game 0-2.

Last season, the Cowboys had the worst starting field position of any team in the NFL, and the issue continued in game one of 2026. Dallas kick returns went for 25, 17, 31, 24, and 25, for an average of 24 yards per return. They also had a penalty on the second return of the game. The punter had a good game, averaging nearly 50 yards per punt, and both punts landed inside the 20. Brandon Aubrey missed one of his three extra points.

The kickers are both All-Pro players and should continue to perform well, but the return game falloff is a significant problem. KaVontae Turpin is a multiple-time All-Pro, but since John Fassel left and Nick Sorensen took the job, the return game has been awful. Putting the offense behind in the field position battle has to be limited. The Cowboys defense and special teams set up their offense to require perfection, and that isn't possible for 17 games a year.

articles.title: Greatness and Joy: Waterdogs Dominate PLL Title Behind Kirst's MVP Performance
articles.summary: (Inside Lacrosse Photo: Dan Aburn) Happy Birthday, CJ Kirst: you are officially the face of lacrosse. The Philadelphia Waterdogs won the Premier Lacrosse Lea...
articles.body:
Happy Birthday, CJ Kirst: you are officially the face of lacrosse.

The Philadelphia Waterdogs won the Premier Lacrosse League championship Sunday in a dominant 14-4 performance over the Denver Outlaws inside Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, N.J.

Kirst, the regular season MVP, was named MVP of the championship game with five goals and two assists. His seven points tied the PLL record in a championship.

He did it with a smile on his face that's been there since at least May 2025 when he led the Cornell Big Red to their first title in nearly 50 years on the heels of the best scoring season in NCAA history. It continued with a Tewaaraton trophy, then an NLL championship and Rookie of the Year, a PLL single-season scoring record, a PLL MVP and now a PLL Championship MVP on his 24th birthday.

And in typical Kirst fashion, it came with an infectious positivity and the rare combo of individual dominance and team-first deference.

"This means everything. It's something we always talk about, is you compete for a reason," said Kirst in an interview with Quint Kessenich postgame. "I'm just so fortunate to be on this stage and so fortunate to be in New Jersey winning for them. So excited and through the roof."

There was no phase in which the Waterdogs were outplayed.

Bill Tierney, the most decorated men's lacrosse coach of all time managed a gem. Zach Currier, the Midfielder of the Year, had a do-everything performance. Michael Sowers, Kirst's strongest competition for league MVP (and Attackman of the Year), QBed the offense to two goals and two assists. The defense held a quartet of Tewaaraton winners to a lifeless performance.

"I learned how to be a leader and competitor," Kirst said of playing for Tierney. "He brings it every day, every phone call, every Zoom call. He's going to do whatever it takes to win, and he lives that."

Kirst struck first with Sowers hung up on X, waiting patiently to find his linemate cut around the action inside and score 5-hole.

But Denver's Luke Wierman won the face-off forward for the second-straight draw, this time hitting the corner after a burst of speed. Currier made sure Philly got it back, though: He swooped up the next face-off with one hand and flipped it back to Alex Stathakis who finished with a twister — making it two goals in eight seconds. Denver's Jake Bernhardt floated to just inside the arc to finish a pass from Dalton Young, but 33 seconds later Currier got open in the high slot to finish Sowers' pass with one second left on the shot clock.

The ping-pong back and forth stopped, but the pace didn't. A clean save from rookie goalie Sean Byrne led to a long pass to Brendan Staub streaking through the middle and a pole goal with defenders draped on him.

Kirst swept across the top to finish from Silas Richmond and make it 5-2. Then 23 seconds later, the speedy Kyle Lewis swept hard only for Kirst to get left along in the slot and go up 6-2.

Currier punctuated the quarter with another big play: Stathakis led him with a face-off win, then Currier grabbed it and tip-toed across the crease and in.

The Outlaws switched Mike Manley, the oldest player in the league, the Leadership Award winner who has yet to win a title, off Kirst for a bit to allow Ben Randall to take the challenge. The result was the same, with Kirst starting the second looping up top and scoring on a shot that hit Logan McNaney.

The Waterdogs finished the half up 10-4, the only assertiveness from Denver's group of superstars being a Brennan O'Neill bully dodge underneath.

The Outlaws defense kept it respectable in the second half. But the Waterdogs' defense of Kenny Brower, Marcus Hudgins and Gavin Adler didn't give an inch. Denver did not score in the second half. O'Neill, Pat Kavanagh, Bernhardt and Logan Wisnauskas were held to 2-of-16.

The performance was punctuated in the fourth. Randall tried to clear early in the quarter, but Sowers stuck to him like glue. He passed it along, but Kirst extended his stick to grab it in the air, passing back to Sowers for the easy dunk on the rainy road to a championship.

Tierney, the seven-time NCAA champion, earned his first pro title. Byrne finished undefeated in a rookie season in which he went from undrafted to midyear starter. He made 11 saves. Rookies Richmond (1G, 1A) and Matt Collison (1G) scored. The veteran Kieran McArdle added a goal.

"Confidence, confidence," Kirst attributed the win. "We had rookies come in, people questioned us being able to do it. … It just trickled out from our veterans all the way down. Everyone's got that confidence."

articles.title: 10 lowest-graded FSU players from Week 3 loss to Alabama
articles.summary: PFF’s postgame grades highlighted several Florida State players who struggled in the Seminoles’ 50-36 loss to Alabama.
articles.body:
Florida State 's 50-36 loss to the No. 8 Alabama Crimson Tide exposed problems in several areas, and Pro Football Focus' postgame grades reflected those struggles. The Seminoles surrendered 567 total yards, including 247 on the ground, while Alabama erased an early 21-6 FSU lead and scored 44 points over the final three quarters.

PFF's lowest overall grades were spread between the offense and defense, with several Florida State players receiving marks below 50.0. Here are the 10 lowest-graded Seminoles from the loss, according to PFF's Week 3 reports.

Graham rounded out the bottom 10 with a 51.8 overall defensive grade in 35 snaps. His 81.8 tackling grade was a notable bright spot, but his coverage and pass-rush marks finished at 51.7 and 55.2, respectively.

Diggs finished with a 50.5 defensive grade across 40 snaps. His strongest individual mark was a 71.1 tackling grade, while PFF graded his run defense at 51.2 and pass rush at 53.0.

Bowling was on the field for all 67 offensive snaps and earned a 49.9 overall grade. His pass-blocking grade came in at 27.7, while he received a 52.1 mark as a run blocker.

Anderson received a 49.6 defensive grade over 43 snaps. PFF graded him at 58.2 as a pass rusher, but his 23.7 tackling mark was among the lowest on the defense.

Richard led Florida State with a career-high 12 tackles, but PFF evaluated his overall performance at 48.9 across 59 snaps. His tackling grade was 62.1, while his run-defense mark finished at 36.3.

Jones played 43 defensive snaps and received a 48.7 overall grade. His lowest individual marks came against the run at 35.5 and as a tackler at 21.7.

Riles finished with a 46.6 overall offensive grade on 34 snaps. PFF gave him a 51.6 receiving mark, but his 29.7 pass-blocking grade brought down his overall evaluation.

Gbayor earned a 44.5 defensive grade over 33 snaps. His marks included 58.6 against the run, 51.5 in tackling and 42.6 in coverage.

Chaplin played all 67 offensive snaps and finished with a 36.6 overall grade. His biggest issue came in pass protection, where PFF graded him at 20.8, compared with a 62.9 run-blocking mark.

Barker received Florida State's lowest overall grade at 30.0 across 51 defensive snaps. PFF gave him a 34.3 run-defense grade, 26.0 tackling grade, and a 33.6 coverage grade.

articles.title: Jadan Baugh carries the load to earn him offensive player of the game
articles.summary: After Jadan Baugh's stellar performance in the conference opener against the Auburn Tigers, he is named our offensive player of the game.
articles.body:
Florida 's first real test this season came against the Auburn Tigers on Saturday. Despite playing inferior competition the first two weeks of the season, the Gators' offense was still operating like a well-oiled machine.

The Orange and Blue left Jordan-Hare Stadium with a 44-39 win. Plenty of penalties set this team back on drives and put them in positions to start drives further than expected, but they were still able to march the field multiple times to find the end zone.

Aaron Philo commanded the offense and served as a leader for the men who took the field, but without the workhorse back that is Jadan Baugh, Florida's offense may have stalled in a few of those drives. For his efforts, Baugh earned Gators Wire's offensive player of the game for Week 3.

The All-SEC running back has done nothing but meet and exceed preseason expectations. In his SEC opener, he rushed for 162 yards and scored three times. Two of his touchdowns were 33 and 53 yards long, showing he's not just a bruiser and can explode for big gains.

Among all running backs in the country who have played at least three games this season, Baugh is the highest-graded player at his position, according to PFF.

PFF also lists Baugh's breakaway percentage as the highest, showing his able to make defenders miss a routine.

What is making the Florida running backs season so impressive is his efficiency. So far this season, Baugh is tied for first in rushing touchdowns with eight. He is also second in total rushing yards despite having significantly fewer carries than the leading rusher.

Baugh's early-season efficiency will be costly as Florida gets deep into conference play, but for now, it earns him his second Gators Wire offensive player of the game.

articles.title: Man Utd salvage Fulham draw as pressure mounts on Carrick
articles.summary: Matheus Cunha strikes late as Manchester United seal a 1-1 draw at Fulham, but pressure mounts on Michael Carrick.
articles.body:
Manchester United rescued a 1-1 draw against Fulham thanks to Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser on Sunday, but the pressure is mounting on boss Michael Carrick after their latest lacklustre display.

Carrick’s football side were in dire need of a victory at Craven Cottage, but instead left grateful for a point.

United fell behind in the second half to a farcical own goal from Lisandro Martinez, who diverted the ball into his own net after Senne Lammens had saved Calvin Bassey’s shot.

Although Cunha’s last-gasp leveller spared United from a third successive defeat, there was little reason for celebration for Carrick and his beleaguered team.

United have just one win in five Premier League matches and already trail leaders Manchester City by 10 points.

They have lost three of their first seven games in all competitions this season and head into the international break with Carrick under intense scrutiny.

Carrick has insisted that he does not care about his future at Old Trafford.

But after successive gut-punch defeats against Manchester City and Brighton, this was another setback to his reeling regime.

Shell-shocked by Erling Haaland’s winner for City in last weekend’s derby – which the referees’ governing body later admitted should have been disallowed – United blew a 2-0 lead against Brighton in the League Cup third round on Wednesday.

Barely escaping with a draw against second-from-bottom Fulham was another indignity in a season already full of forgettable moments for United.

Expected to at least match last season’s third-place finish, United have gone backwards since Carrick was appointed as manager on a permanent basis following his successful interim spell.

United return to action with a home game against bottom-of-the-table Tottenham on October 10, with Carrick and Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi both desperate for a win that would turn the tide.

Foreshadowing their afternoon of struggle, United were fortunate not to fall behind in the opening moments when Fulham forward Gonzalo Garcia dragged his shot wide from a dangerous position.

That narrow escape triggered a response from United as Bruno Fernandes picked out Martinez for a stinging strike from the edge of the penalty area, forcing Bernd Leno to make a superb save.

United went close again when Cunha pulled his pass back to Fernandes, whose fierce strike cannoned off the post.

But United were jittery at the back, and Josh King’s half-volley forced a good save from Lammens before the goalkeeper denied Sander Berge with another smart stop.

Oscar Bobb should have beaten Lammens moments later, but he was off target with a golden opportunity to break the deadlock.

With United far too open, Fulham poured forward in waves in the closing minutes of the first half.

Lammens had to claw away another blast from King, then raced off his line to frustrate Alex Iwobi as the pressure mounted.

United’s lack of drive and cutting edge, combined with some shambolic defending, provided a fatal cocktail that led to Fulham’s opener.

After Cunha carelessly conceded possession deep inside United’s half, Carrick’s men were slow to react as Bassey unloaded a powerful strike that was palmed out by Lammens.

Martinez tried to clear the ball, but his bizarrely mistimed swipe directed it back into his own net via a deflection off the despairing Lammens.

Leno kept out Bryan Mbeumo’s curler and plunged to his left to save Cunha’s low drive as United tried desperately to salvage a point.

United’s late flurry brought an equaliser in the 89th minute.

Cunha tried his luck from distance, and his shot took a wicked deflection off David Affengruber. For once, Carrick’s luck was in.

articles.title: Eagles-Titans analysis: Hurts recovers, defense controls first half
articles.summary: Philadelphia leads Tennessee 14-10 at halftime after losing Saquon Barkley early and surviving a Jalen Hurts’ interception
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles controlled most of the first half against the Tennessee Titans , but an injury to Saquon Barkley and one costly decision by Jalen Hurts prevented them from building a commanding lead. Philadelphia led 14-10 at halftime after outgaining Tennessee 210-96, producing 15 first downs and possessing the football for 21 minutes, 50 seconds. Hurts completed 14 of 17 passes for 141 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Tank Bigsby replaced Barkley and scored Philadelphia's first touchdown before Hurts connected with DeVonta Smith for a 22-yard score.

Here are the biggest takeaways from the first half.

Saquon Barkley 's injury becomes the most important development

Barkley was slow to get up after his first carry and left the field immediately. He appeared to favor his left arm before entering the medical tent. He did not receive another first-half snap. Barkley's status becomes Philadelphia's primary concern regardless of Sunday's final result. The Eagles entered the afternoon intending to establish their running game against a Tennessee defense that allowed 152 yards in Week 1.

Instead, Bigsby and Will Shipley had to carry the backfield.

Shipley played 22 snaps and rushed seven times for 24 yards. Bigsby played 17 snaps and carried 10 times for 27 yards and one touchdown. Neither produced Barkley's explosiveness, but both helped the offense maintain its identity.

Hurts recovered from a brutal interception

Philadelphia's opening possession was methodical until Hurts made the half's most damaging mistake. Amani Hooker stepped in front of his end-zone throw and returned the interception 92 yards. Makai Lemon prevented a defensive touchdown by chasing down Hooker, but Cam Ward scored on a fourth-and-goal sneak to give Tennessee a 7-0 lead.

The turnover created Tennessee's only touchdown despite Philadelphia's defense forcing a three-and-out on its opening series. Hurts responded well. Excluding the interception, he completed 14 of 16 attempts for 141 yards and one touchdown. He remained poised against pressure and capped Philadelphia's third possession with a well-placed 22-yard touchdown pass to Smith.

The quarterback's recovery was encouraging. The original decision cannot be repeated in the second half.

Dontayvion Wicks keeps delivering in critical situations

Wicks caught all four of his targets for 54 yards, with each reception moving the chains or keeping a scoring drive alive.

His catches included gains of 27 yards on third-and-12, 7 yards on third-and-4, 5 yards on fourth-and-2, and 15 yards on another third-and-12. Wicks has quickly become one of Hurts' most trusted options on money downs. Tennessee had opportunities to end Philadelphia's long possessions but repeatedly lost Wicks within the design of Sean Mannion's passing game.

His production was not built on empty volume. Every catch mattered.

The Eagles ran 41 offensive plays to Tennessee's 23 and controlled possession for nearly 22 minutes. Philadelphia converted six of nine third downs and its only fourth-down attempt. Its two touchdown drives lasted 11 plays and 14 plays, respectively, consuming a combined 14:11. The Eagles also finished the half with 210 yards to Tennessee's 96.

Those numbers should have produced a larger advantage. Hurts' interception and Tennessee's late 37-yard field goal kept the Titans within four points despite being thoroughly outplayed for most of the half.

Philadelphia must turn its statistical control into greater separation after halftime.

Makai Lemon is becoming more comfortable

Lemon's pursuit prevented Hooker from completing a 100-yard interception return, but his contributions extended beyond that effort play. The rookie consistently generated separation, including a third-down reception after Wicks cleared space. Lemon looked more comfortable releasing against coverage and finding openings within the design.

He caught three passes for 30 yards during the half after finishing his debut with two receptions for minus-1 yard.

Lemon's willingness to block, pursue and contribute without being the featured receiver has already earned Philadelphia's trust. His route running may start to earn him a larger offensive role.

The defense controlled Tennessee until the final minute

Philadelphia forced a three-and-out on Tennessee's opening possession and allowed only 40 yards before the Titans' final drive of the half. Nolan Smith Jr. recorded a sack, while the Eagles limited Ward to five completions on nine attempts for 63 yards. Tennessee finished with four first downs and converted two of six third downs.

Calvin Ridley committed a personal foul that turned a promising possession into third-and-16 and eventually forced a punt. The defense's only touchdown allowed came after Hooker's interception return gave Tennessee possession at Philadelphia's 12. Ward needed four plays to cover the short field. Tennessee finally generated an explosive sequence before halftime when Ward connected with Elic Ayomanor and Tyjae Spears gained 28 yards on a screen. Joey Slye 's 37-yard field goal cut Philadelphia's lead to 14-10.

The Eagles controlled the half, but Barkley's injury and the interception ensured meaningful work remained in the final two quarters.

articles.title: Todd Monken's fourth-down decision allows Bucs to take 9-6 halftime lead
articles.summary: The Browns and the Buccaneers both look like teams with a lot of improvements to make if they’re going to be competitors this season.
articles.body:
The Browns and the Buccaneers both look like teams with a lot of improvements to make if they're going to be competitors this season.

But a poor coaching decision by Cleveland's Todd Monken allowed Tampa Bay to take a 9-6 lead at halftime.

When the Browns faced fourth-and-1 from their own 34 with 2:50 left in the second quarter, the club's defense had been playing well. The team had allowed just five first downs and picked off quarterback Baker Mayfield. But Monken still elected to go for it, calling a Quinshon Judkins run up the middle.

It was easily stuffed for a turnover on downs, giving Tampa Bay the ball deep in Cleveland territory.

But the underwhelming Buccaneers offense didn't do much with the opportunity. While the team advanced down to the Cleveland 11, the unit stalled from there with a screen pass that went backward, followed by two Mayfield incompletions.

Chase McLaughlin hit his third field goal of the half to give the Buccaneers a three-point lead.

Mayfield is just 9-of-15 for 45 yards with an interception. Tampa Bay has just seven first downs, 126 yards, and is 3-of-8 on third down.

Cleveland has registered three sacks — one each from Grant Delpit, Ronnie Hickman, and Mason Graham.

On the other side, Cleveland's offense has done next to nothing. The team has just three first downs, 59 total yards, and is 0-of-6 on third down — and the Browns are somehow still in it. The club has also had several penalty issues, with six accepted for 50 yards.

Deshaun Watson, who may be making his final start in an orange helmet, is 7-of-9 for 55 yards. Judkins has 18 yards on nine carries, with the Tampa Bay defense clearly keying in on him. Harold Fannin has one 21-yard reception, which was Watson's best throw of the day so far.

The Buccaneers will have a chance to get things going early in the third quarter, as they'll receive the second-half kickoff.

articles.body:
UPDATE: Eagles star Saquon Barkley returned on the first play of the third quarter against the Titans.

NASHVILLE, Tenn.— Eagles running back Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger on Philadelphia 's first offensive play on on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium.

Barkley suffered the injury while getting tackled by Titans star Jeffery Simmons . Simmons brought Barkley down for no gain.

Barkley is questionable to return against Tennessee, the team announced. He spent most of Philadelphia's first offensive drive in the medical tent. After being evaluated, he jogged into the locker room.

If Barkley doesn't return, the Eagles will lean on backup running backs Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley to carry the load. The Eagles could struggle to run the ball with Barkley sidelined.

articles.title: Report: Arsenal tracking Nwaneri’s Dortmund teammate as striker search continues
articles.summary: Arsenal are reportedly keeping a close eye on Borussia Dortmund forward Maximilian Beier as Andrea Berta continues to assess potential additions to Mikel Art...
articles.body:
Arsenal are reportedly keeping a close eye on Borussia Dortmund forward Maximilian Beier as Andrea Berta continues to assess potential additions to Mikel Arteta's attack.

The Gunners ended the summer without landing another major attacking target after their pursuit of Julian Alvarez came to nothing, something we discussed recently when looking at whether Arsenal's transfer gamble could point towards another big signing in the coming January transfer window.

It appears the search has certainly not stopped.

Arsenal have reportedly watched Beier for 12 months

According to TEAMtalk , Arsenal scouts have been monitoring Beier for around 12 months and have been impressed by the 23-year-old German international. The report claims he is now firmly on the club's radar as they assess their future attacking options.

Beier joined Borussia Dortmund from Hoffenheim in 2024 for a fee of around €30million and has since registered 20 goals and 14 assists for the Bundesliga club.

One of the obvious attractions for Arsenal appears to be his versatility.

Although primarily a central striker, Beier can also operate from either flank or behind the main forward. That flexibility could certainly appeal to Arteta, whose attacking players are regularly required to perform more than one role.

Interestingly, the report also suggests Arsenal scouts see similarities between Beier and Kai Havertz , particularly in their movement, intelligence and ability to find space rather than simply operating as conventional number nines.

Nwaneri link gives Arsenal another chance to watch Beier

Arsenal already have another reason to be paying close attention to Dortmund this season, with Ethan Nwaneri spending the campaign there on loan .

The Gunners will naturally be monitoring the youngster's progress closely, potentially giving their recruitment team further opportunities to watch Beier at close quarters.

Manchester United and Tottenham are also reported to be paying attention to him.

For now, therefore, Beier is one to add to an increasingly interesting list of attacking players being monitored by Arsenal for a potential January transfer.

articles.summary: Fans will be thrilled to see the Kenyan back in London this December.
articles.body:
With the 2027 PDC WC just a few months away, players are slowly starting to secure their spots at the tournament.

In the coming weeks, we will see international qualifiers, giving players from all corners of the country a chance to join a European-dominated field.

On Sunday, a North African PDC WC qualifier was held, as the first of two African players heading to Alexandra Palace was determined.

Ally Pally fan favorite David Munyua qualifies for 2027 PDC World Darts Championship

2026 PDC WC qualifier David Munyua will be returning to the biggest event in darts this year for the second straight time in his career.

The Kenyan booked his spot with an 8-7 thrilling win against Evans Njuguna in the final of the qualifier.

Munyua was pretty consistent throughout the qualifying event, with the exception of one match, averaging in the low 80s from the round of 32 and on.

Munyua became a fan favorite at last year's WC when he upset Mike De Decker in the first round.

He trailed 2-0 in sets that game, but managed to beat the Belgian, in what was viewed as one of the best upset wins in darts history.

The 2027 PDC WC kicks off on Dec. 11 and concludes on Jan. 3.

articles.title: Oklahoma football news: Brent Venables' response to dreadful offense
articles.summary: Oklahoma football came away with a 14-6 win against New Mexico, but it wasn’t the best performance for the team. Head coach Brent Venables definitely wasn’t...
articles.body:
Oklahoma football came away with a 14-6 win against New Mexico, but it wasn't the best performance for the team. Head coach Brent Venables definitely wasn't satisfied with what he saw, especially from the offense. After the game, Venables was asked if he thinks the offense has anything to hang its hat on.

"No. Did you watch the game?" Venables said via George Stoia III of On3.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Oklahoma finished with 299 total yards of offense, but finished with seven penalties. John Mateer had a solid game with 238 passing yards for two touchdowns and two interceptions, but it was obvious that the team wasn't able to get much going on that side of the ball.

If New Mexico made a few more plays, there's a chance that they could've come up with a big upset, but Oklahoma's defense did what they were supposed to do.

All eyes were on offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle after the game, and many are questioning if he's the man for the job to help Oklahoma. Venables still has faith in the play caller, and he showed that in the presser as well.

"I'm not going to talk about confidence. He's our offensive coordinator… We have to be better," Venables said.

It'll be interesting to see what Oklahoma does to turn things around next week when they face Georgia, but that's not going to be an easy matchup. The offense has to find a way to get into a rhythm, and it'll start with Mateer and how he commands the offense.

articles.title: Georgia Tech Wins First Game As Mendoza And Haynes Shine
articles.summary: Georgia Tech finally breaks its losing streak with a dominant 44-11 win. Mendoza and Haynes combine for six scores, but the players remain critical of their...
articles.body:
Georgia Tech fans can finally exhale after the Yellow Jackets secured their first win of the season. The team crushed Mercer 44-11 on Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, in Atlanta. This victory snapped a painful 0-2 start that had left the city worried. According to Atlanta News First , the offense exploded for 44 points while the defense held firm. The score tells the whole story of a team that found its rhythm at last.

Alberto Mendoza directed the offense with 15 completions out of 21 attempts, totaling 249 yards and three touchdowns. This marked his third start for the program. Running back Justice Haynes added 167 total yards and scored three times himself. Haynes scored twice by running, and he also reached the end zone via a pass. These numbers show a duo that is finally clicking together. Per Georgia Tech Athletics , the combination of Mendoza's arm and Haynes' legs proved too much for the opponent.

The most surprising part of this win is how critical the stars are of their own performance. Even with six combined touchdowns, neither player feels they played perfectly. Mendoza admitted that game reps help players get comfortable. He believes experience helps him read defenses faster. "The more reps I get, the more snaps under center, the more different coverages I see, different disguises, different pressures, I think I start to identify those more and faster," he added.

Justice Haynes took an even harder look in the mirror despite his huge game. This humility is rare in college sports but essential for growth. The team needs this drive to keep improving as the season goes on. According to Atlanta News First, Haynes believes the group is moving in the right direction.

This win changes the narrative for Georgia Tech immediately. The team is no longer searching for answers but refining what works. According to Atlanta News First, Head coach Brent Key noted the Yellow Jackets have much to build upon. The future looks bright if this momentum holds. Yahoo Sports noted that the offensive balance was the key to dismantling Mercer. The city can now look ahead with hope instead of dread. The stats prove the offense works, but the players' attitude proves the culture is right.

articles.title: This cartoony Patriots-Steelers sequence that leads to astonishing 4th-and-43 is must-watch clip
articles.summary: With points proving hard to come by in the early moments of the Patriots and Steelers' Week 2 tilt, spectators had to seek out alternate sources of joy than...
articles.body:
With points proving hard to come by in the early moments of the Patriots and Steelers ' Week 2 tilt, spectators had to seek out alternative sources of joy other than the scoreboard.

Neutral observers might have found one in the form of a curious incident that saw the game take on a more humorous disposition partway through the second quarter.

Inside the cartoony Patriots - Steelers fumble sequence that resulted in 4th-and-43

Deep in the second quarter, Pittsburgh looked poised to potentially put some points on the board. Mike McCarthy's side ambled across the 50-yard-line, embarking on a pilgrimage that put it within a few yards of the red zone.

On third-and-seven, Rodgers dropped back to pass, hoping to part with the oblong orb and send his side careening further towards New England 's end zone. Instead, he was swept away in a tempest of navy-clad bodies, releasing the ball upon contact from Christian Elliss . The ball bumbled once it met the ground, dancing some 36 yards behind the line of scrimmage.

New England appeared the likelier of the two teams to recoup the ugly thing. Dre'Mont Jones and Christian Gonzalez each caressed the apparatus for a fleeting moment.

She was unwilling to be tamed, though. The ball slipped from both of their grasps, eventually settling at the 39-yard line. Troy Fautanu was the biggest beneficiary from the Marx Brothers-like sequence; the Steelers offensive lineman flailed to the ground to recover the ball, lying supine before being greeted by other bodies.

It was cartoonish, immature, anxiety-inducing and outrageous. It was also eye-catching — the sight of seeing the ball giving way to its tumbleweed-like intentions proved noteworthy, even if the incident that spurned the alteration didn't.

articles.title: ‘Part of my DNA’: Stephen Fleming sends clear message on facing Australia in Ashes as England’s new Test coach
articles.summary: With Stephen Fleming ready to take over England's Test duties, he made it clear that defeating Australia also brings him joy as a New Zealander.
articles.body:
Stephen Fleming said facing Australia in the Ashes is part of his cricketing DNA.

The former New Zealand skipper described the chance to lead England into the series as a dream come true.

Stuart Broad said Fleming's clear enthusiasm for the challenge was striking.

Stephen Fleming is as eager to beat the Aussies in the Ashes as England's Test coach

Stephen Fleming has barely settled into the England job, but he has already made clear where his priorities sit. Speaking to Michael Atherton, the new Test head coach was reminded that next summer's Ashes are now only a handful of matches away. And his response left no doubt about how much the series means to him personally.

Fleming himself has played 14 Tests against the mighty Australians of the 1990s and 2000s. He also had to retire without ever tasting victory against the Aussies. That's a frustration shared by generations of New Zealand cricketers who have long measured themselves against their much larger neighbour.

For Fleming, too, that's a fire that still burns, and it has motivated an answer that goes well beyond the usual coach-speak about one series among many. Stuart Broad, reacting to the interview afterward, picked out that same moment as the part that struck him most, seeing in it genuine excitement rather than rehearsed enthusiasm for the job.

What Stephen Fleming said about the Ashes being part of his DNA

When asked by former English skipper Michael Atherton whether he needed reminding of what the Ashes mean to England's supporters, Fleming turned the question back towards his own competitive instincts. Atherton was quick to point out that there are just nine Tests remaining for England before the Ashes. In response, the New Zealander remained totally calm.

"Yeah, and you also got to remember that New Zealanders like beating Australians as well. So, that's a good place to start. But it looks, to me as a cricket lover, in part of my DNA to be involved in an Ashes is a dream really to come true. What an opportunity that I'm so privileged to now have," Fleming told Atherton on Sky Sports .

He was candid about needing to manage his emotions around the occasion. "The vision of winning an Ashes is something I might have to suppress. The feelings might be different, but the desire to do it will be 100 per cent the same. And yeah, I have a picture in my mind of what that can look like, and it's pretty good," he added.

But while he remains realistic about what his team can achieve next summer, he is no less excited by the opportunity to defeat Australia in the Ashes.

Why Stuart Broad picked out the same line

Reflecting on the interview afterward, Broad zeroed in on Fleming's Ashes comments as the moment that told him the most about the new coach's mindset heading into the job.

"I enjoyed listening to a lot of his quotes. I think my favourite was New Zealanders like beating the Australians, too. Which made me smile, I must say," Broad said.

The former English seamer cheekily mentioned that perhaps the Kiwis don't enjoy beating the Aussies as much as they do, but he still loved Fleming's energy. "Not perhaps quite as much as we do. But he seemed to have a good energy in his voice, right? He seemed excited to do the job," Broad said.

That reading fits the broader picture of how Fleming has presented himself since taking the role. For someone who spent his playing career falling agonisingly short against Australia, the chance to defeat them has now presented itself to Fleming once again. The only difference is that, instead of the pitch, this time Fleming will stay in the dugout.

With an obvious personal stake in the outcome, Fleming's motivation goes beyond simply doing a professional job well. Now, whether that motivation translates into results next summer remains to be seen, but few will doubt its sincerity.

articles.title: Chicago Bears follow historic Week 1 with disastrous half vs Vikings
articles.summary: The Bears followed a historic Week 1 victory, in which they scored 59 points, with epic sloppiness in the first half against the Vikings.
articles.body:
CHICAGO – As an encore for their historic Week 1 victory, in which the offense scored 59 points, the Chicago Bears presented … epic sloppiness.

The Bears' offensive operation, confronting rainy conditions during the first half fo the home opener against the Minnesota Vikings , was plagued by miscues that resulted in three first-half points and seven penalties for 53 yards. Center Garrett Bradbury , acquired this offseason from the New England Patriots after the sudden retirement of Drew Dalman , was the culprit four times (three holding, one false start).

Indeed, the Vikings' defensive front of Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins , Levi Drake Rodriguez and Jalen Redmond all held their own against the Bears' offensive line that paved the way for 291 yards on the ground and six rushing touchdowns against the Carolina Panthers last week.

During one particularly brutal stretch of play near the two-minute warning in the second quarter on Sunday, the Bears reached the red zone with a Caleb Williams completion to tight end Colston Loveland . Just as it looked like middle of field was opening up for the passing attack at critical moment, that progress was called back due to an illegal shift – an example of the operational woes that head coach Ben Johnson has bemoaned since taking over in 2025.

Fans started booing when referees threw a flag for one of Bradbury's holding offences, and Williams' intentional grounding penalty – on a throwaway attempt that didn't make it past the line of scrimmage – didn't help. And neither did a false start coming out of two-minute warning.

Minnesota carried a 6-3 lead into the locker room at halftime.

"I'll probably be a lot more fresh," said Donald on his reduced snap count. "I'll probably be fresh. It's a long year, long season. Like I said, we have a lot of good football players out here. My game plan is, however it's going to be, I'm going out go out there and play hard. And when I need a break, tap out, let the next guy go out there and eat, and I'll be right back. I think we have a good game plan to get myself going and get this team going. Whatever that role is, I'm ready for it. I'm excited about it and I'm just going to do it."

With Myles Garrett missing the next four games due to injury and his placement on injured reserve, Los Angeles can ill-afford for Donald to get hurt. The good news is that Kobie Turner , Poona Ford , Braden Fiske , and others are more than talented enough to allow the three-time Defensive Player of the Year to do what he does best: hunt down quarterbacks.
