articles.title: Kara Lawson on overcoming assumptions in time coaching with Boston Celtics
articles.summary: Lawson worked hard to keep her status as a female coach from being a distraction. But not everyone helped with that mission, unfortunately.
articles.body:
When current-day Duke Women's Basketball head coach Kara Lawson was working as an assistant coach for the Boston Celtics , she did not want the fact that she was a woman to be a distraction despite being one of a handful around the NBA in such a role and the first in history for the Celtics. But there were moments when that was out of her hands, the assumptions of others working in her ambit working against her in ways that simply would not have happened had she been a man in that role.

Lawson shared an example of how this would happen from time to time in away venues where the event security would be unaware of her identity as one of Boston's assistant coaches in a recent interview . "I think some of the harder moments were probably when you'd be in away arenas, because they wouldn't believe you were a part of the staff and they wouldn't let me on the court because I didn't have a credential," she explained.

"But coaches don't wear credentials," Lawson continued. "We just go from the locker room to the to the court, and the security would stop me a lot."

"And I would literally be walking next to a fellow assistant coach that was a male that didn't have a credential," she added, "but they wouldn't stop them they would always stop me."

"And then they would ask where my credential is. And I say, 'Well, I don't have one'. They say, 'Well, you can't come on the court'. And then the assistant coach that was with me would be like, 'No, she's a coach. And then they still wouldn't let me'. And they go get a supervisor. And then, so then I'm late to the bench because I couldn't get on (court). So it would be things like that, that people wouldn't think that. I was a coach."

"That was usually at the away arenas," said Lawson. "Obviously, in the home arena in Boston, all the security and ushers knew who I was."

articles.title: Bill Belichick Confronts Program Turmoil After Silent Press Conference
articles.summary: Bill Belichick watched North Carolina’s biggest opportunity turn into a 28–20 loss to Clemson. The Tar Heels led 17–6 at halftime, but their defense then all...
articles.body:
Bill Belichick watched North Carolina's biggest opportunity turn into a 28–20 loss to Clemson. The Tar Heels led 17–6 at halftime, but their defense then allowed 22 straight points.

The loss came two days after a UNC investigation ended and his son, Steve Belichick, resigned as defensive coordinator. Reporters asked Bill Belichick about the situation and his response wasn't welcoming.

Bill Belichick shuts down media after collapse against Clemson

North Carolina controlled the first half at Death Valley, then lost its defensive grip after halftime. Clemson scored on drives of 88, 92, 68, and 44 yards, turning a 17-6 deficit into a 28-20 win. Brian Belichick handled defensive play-calling after Steve's departure, but the secondary could not stop Clemson's second-half progress.

Asked about the program's turmoil after the loss, Bill said, "I am just focused on the Clemson game run. It just ended 10 minutes ago," according to the postgame press conference .

A reporter then asked whether the off-field situation made the defeat harder to process. Belichick replied, "Yeah, I just talked about that." He returned to football and gave no details about the probe or his son's exit.

Steve resigned two days before the Clemson game after UNC announced that its internal investigation had concluded. The university said certain actions disregarded Carolina's values and conduct standards, but called them isolated, not systemic.

ESPN reported that the investigation included allegations involving drug use and relationships, but UNC did not specifically connect Steve or former general manager Michael Lombardi to those allegations.

Defensive collapse exposes UNC's struggles following Steve Belichick's exit

Steve's medical leave began on August 6, so UNC had already been operating without its defensive coordinator before his resignation. Bill Belichick and Bob Diaco shared defensive planning duties during that period.

His resignation takes effect on October 27, after his medical leave ends. Media reports connected the timing to the university probe and noted that Michael Lombardi had resigned on September 3.

The arrangement gave UNC time to prepare, but it did not create a permanent replacement. Brian's expanded responsibility now carries greater weight after Clemson exposed the defense's communication and coverage problems.

The staff now has a defined short-term problem. Brian Belichick must help replace Steve's defensive role, and Bill must keep UNC's season on track after Clemson exposed the cost of the transition. The university considers the investigation resolved, but the football consequences remain active.

articles.body:
North Florida hitters did not make a single mistake while destroying Kennesaw State in the final set. The Ospreys went 10 for 14 on attacks with a massive .714 hitting percentage to seal the win. This level of perfection in a deciding fifth set is rare and deadly for any opponent. Kennesaw State fought hard but could not stop the surge when it mattered most.

The match started as a tight fight on the Georgia Southern campus. Neither side could break away as the opening set saw 15 ties and eight lead changes. Kennesaw State finally broke through after a close struggle to take the first set 28-26. Haley Patterson and Ashley Theiss scored the key points to win that set by two points. North Florida bounced back quickly to take the second set 25-22. Kennesaw State rallied later to win the third set 25-20 and take a 2-1 lead.

Olivia Burrage was part of a 6-1 closing run that helped secure that third set win. The Owls held the advantage heading into the fourth set. North Florida opened a large lead before Kennesaw State tried to rally late. Ashlyn Anderson and Patterson scored kills to cut the margin to five points. The Ospreys stopped the comeback to take the set 25-19 and force a final frame. Kennesaw State University Athletics reported the match took place on Sep. 19, 2026.

The fifth set began with North Florida scoring the first three points. An early 4-0 run helped UNF establish an 8-2 advantage. For the remainder, the Ospreys kept control. By hitting .714 in the frame, they secured the 15-5 victory. Kennesaw State had no answer for the Ospreys as the gap grew too wide. In that final set, North Florida tallied 10 kills with zero attack errors on 14 attempts. This efficiency was the difference maker in the hard-fought five-set loss.

Haley Patterson recorded her third 20-plus kill game this season, leading the Owls with 21 kills. She contributed seven digs and three blocks, ending with a team-high 23.5 points. Her effort was not enough to overcome the offensive explosion from the visitors. Kennesaw State Athletics noted the team fought hard but fell short in the end. The loss closed out the non-conference schedule for the Owls.

Head Coach Keith Schunzel spoke about the effort shown by his squad. He said, "We're proud of our team for fighting today the way we did." The team showed heart but the final set numbers tell a harsh story. Kennesaw State will need to fix their defense if they want to win close matches. North Florida proved they can dominate when the pressure is highest.

The Owls will look to build on the 21 kills from Patterson as they move forward. The team must find a way to stop elite hitting percentages like the one UNF posted. Kennesaw State University Athletics confirmed the final score was 3-2 in sets. The match ended with a 15-5 score in the fifth set.

Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush lost a fumble and threw an interception on the first two offensive possessions, and the Panthers also thwarted a fourth down conversion try later in the half. All of that good work allowed them to get into halftime with a 20-3 lead on the road.

Rush's fumble led to the only Panthers touchdown of the first half. Bryce Young moved the team inside the 10-yard-line with a third down strike to wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan and then hit running back Chuba Hubbard for a three-yard score.

A long punt return by Jalen Coker set the Panthers up in Falcons territory later in the first quarter, but the team settle for the first of three Ryan Fitzgerald field goals after their drive stalled out.

The Falcons finally got on the board with 1:07 left in the half, but Young found wide receiver Xavier Legette for a 55-yard gain to put the Panthers in scoring position. He then found tight end Darren Waller in the end zone with 20 seconds to play to extend the lead to 17 points at the break.

articles.title: Todd McLellan Rips Red Wings Veterans After Embarrassing Camp Finale
articles.summary: Todd McLellan sharply criticized Red Wings veterans after Detroit’s final training-camp session, saying the kids out-executed them by a wide margin.
articles.body:
Todd McLellan did not mince words after the Detroit Red Wings wrapped up training camp Sunday.

The coach liked what he saw from the young players. The veterans? Not so much.

McLellan's blunt assessment came after a final camp session in which Detroit's kids outworked, out-executed and outplayed the more established group. With preseason games looming, it was a message the Red Wings' veterans needed to hear.

McLellan Was Not Happy With Detroit's Day

"I wasn't happy with our day today at all," McLellan said. "I was happy with the kids, but I wasn't happy with our day.

"So we've got to take it back up here after their off days and get going and not waste a day."

That is not a coach nitpicking a sloppy drill or one bad shift. McLellan's concern was the standard Detroit set on the final day of camp, and the urgency is understandable.

The Red Wings have spent too many recent seasons watching promising stretches dissolve when the games tightened. Andrew Copp recently said the club cannot accept anything less than the playoffs, while Moritz Seider has stressed that Detroit cannot waste this season .

McLellan's point Sunday was simple: that expectation has to show up in practice before it can show up in the standings.

"The kids were really good," McLellan said. "They worked their butts off, they made plays, they executed better than the veteran players—it wasn't even close.

"So that's a really good sign for our organization. Or maybe it isn't, it depends how you look at it."

There is the dry McLellan twist. Detroit's prospect group providing energy and execution is encouraging, particularly after interim GM Shawn Horcoff identified Carter Mazur, William Wallinder and Michael Brandsegg-Nygaard as players positioned to advance.

But it becomes a problem when the established players fail to match that standard.

McLellan did not identify specific veterans, and it would be unfair to turn his broad critique into a claim about any one player. Still, "it wasn't even close" is about as direct as a coach can be in September.

McLellan added that the organization's challenge is the limited time available to make meaningful evaluations before the season begins.

"The problem that we have is the amount of time we have to truly evaluate," he said.

That puts the pressure on everyone. Veterans must show they are ready to lead, while younger players have a clear opening to force their way into larger roles. Detroit's roster can be found on the official Red Wings roster page , but the depth chart is not set in stone simply because camp is ending.

The Red Wings have talked about being harder to play against, more structured defensively and more urgent in key moments. Sunday's camp finale suggests McLellan believes some of his veterans are still talking about that identity more than they are demonstrating it.

articles.title: Doctor shares details of injury Philadelphia Eagles’ Saquon Barkley suffered vs Tennessee Titans
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles Running Back Saquon Barkley went straight to the locker room with 8:10 seconds left in the first quarter, as he appeared to suffer an inj...
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles Running Back Saquon Barkley went straight to the locker room with 8:10 seconds left in the first quarter, as he appeared to suffer an injury during a play.

This led to instant fear among fans, as Barkley is one of the most important pieces in the Eagles offense.

There was a lot of anticipation to see if he would return to the field, but the team confirmed that his status would be questionable as it was confirmed by them that he was dealing with a stinger.

Doctor Jesse Morse M.D. revealed what this means for Barkley, and stated if he could be seen again in the game against the Tennessee Titans .

"Eagles announced he's dealing with a stinger," tweeted Morse.

"This is an overstretching of one of the nerves coming out of the neck, often, C5 –6. This causes immediate loss of sensation of the upper extremity, leading to the limb immediately going 'limp.' Sometimes pain is involved.

"If this is only one side and he has regained normal function, then he will be able to return. This is the most likely scenario. If this is on both sides (bilateral), then he will be ruled out for the rest of the game and will require a CT and MRI. My suspicion is, he returns with some additional padding around his neck/ shoulder pads. Overall, good news."

Barkley returned from the locker room wearing a Cowboy collar, a molded polyethylene foam neck protection device designed to limit extreme backward head movement.

He currently does not have his helmet on, and the Eagles have brought in Tank Bigsby , who has already scored a touchdown for the team.

The decision to bring Barkley back into the game will be a tough one to make. The team would not want to risk their star RB in this game, but if he shows signs of improvement, they could bring him on later.

articles.title: Gary Neville lambasts Manchester United’s display against Fulham as an ‘absolute disgrace’
articles.summary: Neville also called for Michael Carrick to stop defending his players’ poor performances
articles.body:
Gary Neville criticised Manchester United 's performance during their 1-1 draw with Fulham calling it and 'absolute disgrace'

Matheus Cunha rescued a point for the Red Devils with a deflected strike in the 89th minute after a Lisandro Martinez own goal had sent the Cottagers into the lead.

United took 29 shots throughout the game but were unable to capitalise in the final third and the scrutiny will now increase on manager Michael Carrick after a week of poor performances has seen them lose to Manchester City and Brighton (in the league cup) and now draw with Fulham who began the match bottom of the Premier League table.

The display at Craven Cottage was called out by Neville on Sky Sports commentary as he said the team played the "worst 15 minutes of football" he can remember seeing since watching the team from the age of five.

After the game, Neville explained his reasoning adding: "I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I've never seen a Manchester United team walk, out of possession, as much as that.

"Michael [Carrick] said he was happy with the team's energy, Michael's got to stop defending them. I get why he's defending them, he's loyal and wants his players to work for him. Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I've never seen a Manchester United team, for 15 minutes, walk around out of possession as much as that. No alertness, no liveliness, no sort of on your toes. Just walking when Fulham were in possession."

Neville went further and showcased what needs to change in United's performances by calling out the attacking players who were not excelling in their defensive duties.

"There needs to be a rebalance," Neville continued, "I wish he [Carrick] could play those attacking players but they're going to kill him defensively. Mbeumo and Rashford are too wide and too high, they don't narrow and get back in. You've then got Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield who are a little bit one-paced and Bruno [Fernandes] at times floats around and Cunha floats around a little bit.

"These five or six players are all better with the ball than without the ball and it would be great to see them score loads of goals, concede one or two and go on to win games but there's going to have to be a reset from the point of view of defensive structure.

"There are far too many of them walking on the pitch and thinking they don't have to do the ugly part of the game. Very rarely do I say that a team doesn't work hard or is lacking in effort because that's the ultimate criticism you can give a group of players.

"That first 15 minutes of the second half, well for 60 minutes, Manchester United were an absolute disgrace. Nowhere near good enough without the ball. Nowhere near good enough."

articles.title: ‘They would not let Manchester United lose’: Fulham boss decries refereeing decisions after Premier League stalemate
articles.summary: Alvaro Arbeloa said that ‘every decision’ went in favour of the visitors as they fought back to earn a fortunate 1-1 draw at Craven Cottage
articles.body:
Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has suggested that Manchester United received favourable treatment in Sunday's 1-1 draw at Craven Cottage because of the VAR controversy over Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby .

Fulham went ahead in the 63rd minute after Lisandro Martinez turned into his own net, though United rescued a point late on as Matheus Cunha 's effort deflected past Bernd Leno in the 89th minute.

Both sides wasted chances in a game that was sluggish at times, though there were no particularly controversial calls made by either referee Peter Bankes or the VAR team.

Nevertheless, Arbeloa complained about the refereeing, including a decision to award Harry Maguire a free-kick near halfway just 35 seconds before the equalising goal.

"We were so close. So, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team. Also, we knew what happened last week," said Arbeloa after the full-time whistle.

"We have seen what the referee have been doing in all the matches, so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky.

"You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire; it's a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them and I knew after the game against Man City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here," he said.

Arbeloa was referring to last week's incident in the Manchester derby, where Erling Haaland's winning goal was incorrectly awarded . Pro Ref later issued an apology to Manchester United , with VAR assistant Matt Donohue stood down for this weekend's games.

Sunday's draw was enough to take Fulham out of bottom spot in the Premier League , with the Cottagers climbing into 19th, above Tottenham on goal difference. Their next game comes after the three-week international break, when they will face newly promoted Ipswich at Portman Road on Saturday, 10 October.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Steelers live updates: Score, news, discussion from NFL Week 2
articles.summary: The Patriots will host the Steelers in their 2026 home opener at Gillette Stadium.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots began their 2026 regular season on the wrong foot. Dropping their opener against the world champion Seattle Seahawks , they have started their second campaign under head coach Mike Vrabel with an 0-1 record.

In order to improve to 1-1 and get their first victory of the season, the Patriots will have to defend their home turf against a Pittsburgh Steelers team that did win in Week 1. A win over Pittsburgh would not just mean a return to .500 on the year for New England , though, but also the first W in a home opener since the 2020 season.

Sunday, Sept. 20, 1 p.m. ET | Gillette Stadium (Foxborough, MA) | Broadcast information | Inactives | Game day roster | Weather forecast

The Patriots started the game on defense, and with a quick three-and-out. New England allowed just three combined yards on two Steelers carry, while Aaron Rodgers ' decision to target Christian Gonzalez on the game's first third down led to an incompletion and subsequent punt.

New England's first offensive series started well, with Drake Maye completing passes to DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry to move the unit into Steelers territory. However, the drive came to a quick and disappointing end when Rhamondre Stevenson lost a fumble on his second touch of the day.

Before even starting their next series, a taunting penalty against safety Jalen Ramsey backed the Steelers up at their own 16-yard line. Things did not get better for Rodgers and company from that point on: a short run was followed by Gabe Jacas forcing a throwaway and another incompletion on third down.

Marcus Jones gained 19 yards on his first punt return of the day, allowing the Patriots to begin their second drive on the Pittsburgh 49-yard line. It could have been a quick one, with a 10-yard Jalen Ramsey sack on third down seemingly ending the series. However, a defensive offsides penalty negated the play and gave New England another chance. TreVeyon Henderson took advantage of it: not only did he convert the subsequent 3rd-and-1, he followed it up with a 39-yard touchdown run on the very next play. | Patriots 7 : 0 Steelers

After keeping the Steelers offense in check for the first two series, the unit did find some rhythm on its third. It did not matter: a well-time Robert Spillane blitz forced an incompletion on 3rd-and-6 in New England territory, while Pittsburgh kicker Chris Boswell sent the ensuing 57-yard field goal try wide to the left.

The Patriots offense continued to look good early into its next possession, quickly moving to the Pittsburgh side of the field again. Romeo Doubs caught his first pass as a Patriot, Rhamondre Stevenson converted a 3rd-and-1 after returning to the field following his fumble, and Drake Maye hit Eli Raridon for a 30-yard gain. However, once in the red zone, the unit ran into trouble: a Morgan Moses false start was followed by a 3-yard sack — a play that saw Mike Onwenu suffer an ankle injury. The right guard was carted off the field and quickly ruled out with an ankle injury.

Coming out of the quarter break, another sack led to the Patriots bringing out Andy Borregales . The second-year kickers split the uprights from 30 yards out to extend his team's lead. | Patriots 10 : 0 Steelers

The Patriots had a chance to quickly end the Steelers' first possession of the second quarter, but the offense was able to move the sticks on a 4th-and-1 to keep the series alive. The drive did take 6:50 off the clock and saw Pittsburgh march into potential scoring range, but it ended with a Christian Elliss/Robert Spillane doube-team sack of Aaron Rodgers: the veteran quarterback lost the ball, with neither team able to scoop it up before Steelers left tackle Troy Fautanu did so back at the Pittsburgh 42 — a net loss of 36 yards to set up a 4th-and-43.

New England's offense struggled to find its footing on the next drive, even though a roughing the pass call and 10-yard completion to Mack Hollins allowed the team to move from deep into its own territory to a more comfortable position on the field. However, the series advanced no further than the 38-yard line and eventually ended in a 54-yard Mitch Wishnowsky punt.

New England's defense again did its job on the next drive. Although the Steelers gained two first downs — one via a 14-yard Travis Homer run, the other on a pass interference call against Kevin Byard — they eventually stalled after crossing midfield. An incomplete pass on 3rd-and-9 in the area of Marcus Jones prompted Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy to send out his punting unit for the fourth time in the first half.

The Patriots offense had a chance to double-dip before and after the half, but they struggled to get their offense going in the late second quarter. The series began with a 12-yard sack against Drake Maye, and the team opted to be conservative from that point on. Unfortunately for New England, that approach allowed the Steelers to get the ball back with 40 seconds left on the clock.

While Pittsburgh was unable to turn its next possession into a touchdown, it did manage to cut into the Patriots' 10-point lead when Chris Boswell scored a 56-yard field goal as time expired on the first half. | Patriots 10 : 3 Steelers

The Patriots flirted with a three-and-out to start their first drive of the second half, but Drake Maye moved out the pocket on 3rd-and-5 and found Romeo Dobbs for a 29-yard gain. However, one play later disaster struck: the second-year quarterback attempted a deep pass to Hunter Henry off his back foot and was easily intercepted by linebacker Patrick Queen .

Stay on top of every Patriots update and debate every snap with other diehard fans. Game-day discussion is smoother in the SB Nation app.
